brief_item.title: MemClaw：多Agent LLM系统的受治理共享内存
brief_item.direction_name: Agent Cache、工具结果与记忆共享
brief_item.core_conclusion: 多Agent（fleet）LLM系统共享内存面临未授权泄漏、陈旧传播、矛盾持续与溯源坍塌四类失效。MemClaw提供作用域检索、时序supersession、溯源追踪与策略治理的记忆传播原语，在ArgusFleet上实现四层派生链100%重构、零跨车队泄漏，并主动披露两类负面结果。
brief_item.mechanism: 以系统级原语实现跨车队/Agent的治理共享内存：作用域检索限定可见范围，时序supersession处理陈旧写，溯源追踪记录写入者身份与派生链，策略治理控制记忆传播。通过ArgusFleet评估，强调真实架构洞察与负面结果而非基线benchmarking。
brief_item.result: 四层派生链重构准确率100%、每跳亚秒级；跨车队泄漏为0且保持车队内高可见性；强写模式下写后可见延迟优化为单次搜索往返。同时披露：子租户scope可被直接GET-by-id绕过（已修复），同步近似去重门可能误拒矛盾写。
brief_item.boundary: 仅摘要级证据，全文未获取；ArgusFleet/MemClaw的规模、车队尺寸、模型类型与统计严格性未验证；自研测试床自评，摘要无第三方基线对比；arXiv ID暗示2026-06提交，需确认。
brief_item.project_relevance: 本项目启发：多Agent编排中状态一致性、隔离与溯源是基础设施级关切，其作用域/时序/溯源原语可作为跨域Agent Cache设计的参考。待验证：与现有Agent记忆系统的对比、在更大规模与多模型场景下的表现，以及与DPU/网络侧卸载的结合点。

facts.title: Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
facts.event_hint: Formalizes the 'fleet-memory problem' for multi-agent LLM systems and proposes governed shared-memory primitives (scoped retrieval, temporal supersession, provenance tracking, policy-governed propagation), implemented as MemClaw and evaluated via ArgusFleet.
facts.problem: Multi-agent ('fleet') LLM systems sharing memory face four failure modes: unauthorized leakage, stale propagation, contradiction persistence, and provenance collapse. The paper formalizes this as the 'fleet-memory problem' for cooperating agents.
facts.mechanism: Implements systems-level primitives in a service called MemClaw: scoped retrieval, temporal supersession, provenance tracking, and policy-governed memory propagation across fleets/agents. Evaluated via a system called ArgusFleet, with explicit emphasis on real-world architectural insights and negative results rather than baseline benchmarking.

evidence.claim: Successfully reconstructed 100% of depth-four derivation chains with correct writer identity at sub-second per-hop latency.
Achieved zero cross-fleet leakage while maintaining high intra-fleet visibility.
Under strong write mode, write-to-visible latency optimized to a single search round-trip.
Found that sub-tenant scope could be bypassed on direct GET-by-id requests for agent-scoped credentials (disclosed and remediated during the study).
Found a synchronous near-duplicate gate may prematurely reject contradictory writes before the asynchronous contradiction detector can evaluate them.

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated via the authors' ArgusFleet system; the paper stresses architectural insights and negative results over baseline comparisons. No external baseline systems or standard benchmarks are reported in the abstract. Fleet size, model types, and scale details reside in the full paper (not fetched).
facts.limitations: Abstract-level results only; full body not fetched, so ArgusFleet/MemClaw scale, fleet size, model types, comparison to existing agent-memory systems, and statistical rigor are unverified. Self-reported on the authors' own testbed with no third-party baselines in the abstract. The arXiv ID 2606.24535 implies a 2026-06 submission and should be confirmed.
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to the briefing's Agent-acceleration interest: shared/governed memory across LLM agents is an infrastructural concern for multi-agent orchestration, touching state consistency, isolation, and provenance. It is adjacent to the memory-hardware topics (CXL, KVCache) and has no direct DPU/SmartNIC or optical angle; relevance is via the agent-systems axis rather than the networking/hardware axis.
